newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA SEEK FUNDS FOR SOUTHERN PHILIPPINES.
newsitem.headline: MANILA SEEK FUNDS FOR SOUTHERN PHILIPPINES.

text.p: Manila sought on Friday pledges from 12 countries and other financial institutions to raise 30.9 billion pesos to fund priority projects in southern Philippines, officials said on Friday.
Autonomous Region of Moslem Mindanao (ARMM) governor Nur Misuari told reporters the proposed projects, which included roads, bridges, and ports, were meant to boost the economy in his region.

"The donor countries sympathised with us and (promised) to support us," Misuari told a news conference in General Santos city in southern Philippines after he and other officials presented the priority projects of ARMM in the next three years to the donors.
Among the 12 countries which sent representatives to the meeting were Australia, Japan, United States, Saudi Arabia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.
Bilateral and multilateral institutions such as the World Bank and the United Nations Development Programme also sent representatives.
Misuari said Manila will ask donors to make funding commitments in another meeting to be held in Paris on December 15-17 after reviewing the priority projects of the ARMM.

Misuari, chief of the Moro National Liberation Front, signed a peace pact with the government last September, ending 24 years of revolt for Moslem self-rule that killed more than 125,000 people in southern Philippines.
